meta.title: Governance - Open Healthcare Network Foundation
meta.description: How OHC Foundation separates fiduciary stewardship, technical direction, maintainership, contribution, security, and release governance.

hero.title: Shared infrastructure needs visible decision-making.
hero.body: OHC Foundation exists so CARE is not controlled by one vendor, one donor, one state, or one implementation partner. Governance separates fiduciary stewardship from technical direction while keeping maintainers close to the work.

layers.title: Clear roles for institutional oversight and technical ownership.

board.title: Foundation Board
board.description: Mission, legal, fiduciary, financial, fundraising, risk, and long-term institutional stewardship.

steeringCommittee.title: Technical Steering Committee
steeringCommittee.description: Architecture, technical vision, maintainership, release discipline, and community process oversight.

maintainers.title: Project maintainers
maintainers.description: Day-to-day code review, roadmap execution, issue triage, documentation, and contributor mentorship.

projectGroups.title: Project groups
projectGroups.description: Focused ownership for CARE Core, Apps, standards, security, implementation guides, and clinical workflows.

decisions.title: The board stewards the institution. Technical leaders steward the platform.

policies.title: Governance should be published as operating practice, not branding.

contribution.title: Open contribution
contribution.text: Contributions should flow through public repositories, clear review rules, and a documented maintainer path.

license.title: License clarity
license.text: CARE code is MIT licensed. Documentation and implementation guides should use open content licenses where appropriate.

releases.title: Release governance
releases.text: Stable releases, compatibility expectations, and long-term support direction should be visible to implementers.

security.title: Security reporting
security.text: Vulnerability reporting, disclosure expectations, access-control practices, and auditability are foundation concerns.

conflicts.title: Conflict handling
conflicts.text: The foundation should make conflicts of interest and decision escalation paths explicit as the ecosystem grows.

clinical.title: Clinical accountability
clinical.text: Clinical workflow and AI-related changes need review paths that respect safety, auditability, and human accountability.

security.title: Security, release quality, and clinical safety are governance work.
security.body: Open healthcare infrastructure must be auditable, maintainable, and safe to operate in real clinical settings. Governance connects technical review, responsible disclosure, release compatibility, and human-in-the-loop AI practices.
